1.title: Care & Prayer
1.intro: Everyone shares briefly how they are doing. Pray if appropriate.
flow: Invite each person to share briefly how they are doing.
Listen for needs, burdens, or reasons to celebrate.
Pause and pray when it is appropriate.

2.title: Worship
2.intro: Praise God, give toward needs, and share the Lord’s Supper.
flow: Praise God together.
Give toward needs as they are shared.
Share the Lord’s Supper when appropriate.

3.title: Loving Accountability
3.intro: Look back with honesty and encouragement. This is about obedience, not shame.
flow: Follow
How did you obey what Jesus showed you last time?
Fish

Who did you share with, and what happened?
Open Conversation Box ↗

4.title: Vision: Acts 2 Church Circle
4.intro: Read Acts 2:36–47. Be a part of a church and start a church.

5.title: New Teaching From Scripture
5.intro: Work through the passage as one guided discovery process. These questions are parts of Step 5, not additional checklist items.
flow: Read the command and tell the story.
Read the story together.
Retell the story in your own words.
What do we learn about God?
What do we learn about people?
Pause, pray, and listen.
How will you obey the story?

6.title: Practice: 3 Circles
6.intro: Practice the 3 Circles gospel tool until each person can use it simply and clearly.
flow: Choose who will practice first.
Practice sharing the 3 Circles clearly and simply.
Give brief encouragement and try again if needed.

7.title: Set Goals
7.intro: Choose clear next steps before leaving the gathering.
flow: Follow
What is Jesus asking you to obey before the next gathering?
Fish
Who needs to hear this story?

8.title: Commission with Prayer
8.intro: Pray together and send one another out to obey Jesus.
flow: Pray for the commitments and people that were named.
Ask the Holy Spirit for courage, power, and faithfulness.
Send one another out to obey Jesus.

3.title: Hear the Story
3.intro: Hear the story several ways so everyone can understand and remember it.
3.retell: Retell the story in your own words.

4.title: Discover & Obey
4.intro: Explore the story together, listen to God, and name a clear response.
flow: What do we learn about God?
What do we learn about people?
Pause, pray, and listen.
How will you obey?

5.title: Practice
flow: Choose who will practice first.
Tell the story without reading it.
Give brief encouragement and practice again if needed.

6.title: Follow Goal
6.intro: Decide how you will respond to Jesus before the next gathering.
flow: Follow
What is Jesus asking you to obey this week?

7.title: Fish Goal
7.intro: Name a person who needs hope and make a specific plan to share.
flow: Fish
Who needs to hear this story? When will you share it?

8.title: Pray
8.intro: Pray for the obedience and sharing commitments that were made.
flow: Pray for each Follow Goal.
Pray by name for each person in the Fish Goals.
Ask God for courage, love, and faithfulness.

fear.hint: Use when they say: ‘I’m stressed about money,’ ‘I don’t know how things will work out,’ ‘I’m worried about the future.’
fear.title: Hope Trusts God for Provision
fear.desc: For fear, lack, money stress, and anxiety about the future.
fear.messageTemplate:
That sounds really heavy. I’m sorry you’re dealing with that. I have a short video and a couple simple questions that speak into money stress and worry. It takes about 5 minutes. Would you be open to going through it?

[LINK]

shame.hint: Use when they say: ‘I’ve messed up,’ ‘I feel ashamed,’ ‘I’m not good enough for God.’
shame.title: Hope for the Rejected
shame.desc: For shame, regret, failure, and feeling unworthy of love or forgiveness.
shame.messageTemplate:
Thanks for being honest about that. I have a short story about someone who felt completely unworthy, and how Jesus responded to them. It’s really meaningful and only takes a few minutes. Would you be open to going through it?

[LINK]

running.category: Running from God / Wanting to Come Back
running.hint: Use when they say: ‘I’ve drifted,’ ‘I want to come back to God,’ ‘I feel far from Him.’
running.title: Hope is Waiting for You
running.desc: For those who feel far from God and want to come home.
running.messageTemplate:
I’m really glad you shared that. I have a short story about someone who walked away and what it looked like to come back. It’s really encouraging. Would you be open to going through it?

[LINK]

pride.hint: Use when they say: ‘I’m a good person,’ ‘I don’t really do religion,’ ‘I don’t think I need that.’
pride.title: Hope for the Nonreligious
pride.desc: For self-trust, spiritual pride, or people who think they do not need God.
pride.messageTemplate:
I appreciate you sharing that. I have a short story that speaks to how people approach God and what really matters. It’s simple and only takes a few minutes. Would you be open to going through it?

[LINK]

change.category: Need Life Change / Stuck in Patterns
change.hint: Use when they say: ‘I need to change,’ ‘My life is a mess,’ ‘I’m stuck in unhealthy patterns.’
change.title: Hope Changes Things
change.desc: For people who know something needs to change and want a different direction.
change.messageTemplate:
Thanks for sharing that. I have a short story about someone whose life was stuck in a pattern, and what changed when they encountered Jesus. It’s really practical. Would you be open to going through it?

[LINK]

bitterness.hint: Use when they say: ‘I can’t forgive them,’ ‘I’m still angry,’ ‘I can’t let go of what they did.’
bitterness.title: Hope Forgives
bitterness.desc: For bitterness, grudges, anger, and inability to forgive.
bitterness.messageTemplate:
That kind of situation can be really hard to carry. I have a short story about forgiveness and what it looks like to let go. It’s powerful and only takes a few minutes. Would you be open to going through it?

[LINK]

hopelessness.hint: Use when they say: ‘I’ve lost hope,’ ‘I thought life would be different,’ ‘I’m grieving,’ ‘Nothing is changing.’
hopelessness.title: Hope Rose from the Dead
hopelessness.desc: For grief, disappointment, confusion, and loss of hope.
hopelessness.messageTemplate:
That sounds really difficult. I have a short story about hope in the middle of loss and disappointment. It’s really encouraging and only takes a few minutes. Would you be open to going through it?

[LINK]

crisis.hint: Use when they say: ‘I’m at the end,’ ‘I can’t do this anymore,’ ‘I need help right now.’
crisis.title: Hope Through Death
crisis.desc: For crisis, final-stage desperation, fear, and urgent need for mercy and hope.
crisis.messageTemplate:
I’m really glad you said something. When things feel this intense, it can help to look at a story of someone in a moment of desperation and what happened next. This is short and meaningful. Would you be open to going through it?

[LINK]
